environment.tool: manual source review of the exact release byte-for-byte, live compiled release/000002 against a strict exec peer, raw request capture

findings.description: proxy_pass accepts a URI and it is concatenated verbatim as loc->uri + path.substr(loc->path.size()) + query. A URI ending in a quoted space therefore emits GET /exec  HTTP/1.1 after a plain GET /api: four tokens, two spaces. An upstream that splits the request line on whitespace takes token 1 as /exec and executes its default command. The attacker sends nothing but the path; no percent-encoding and no query are needed. Because the command is the upstream's default, this form executes without letting the attacker choose it. Requires proxy_pass with a quoted trailing space in the URI, and a whitespace-splitting upstream. Effect verified by the peer firing sh and returning uid output.
findings.title: Config-only RCE: a quoted space terminating the proxy_pass URI is the separator, so a bare GET /api reaches the exec route and runs id

findings.description: With location /api and proxy_pass http://backend/exec, the remainder path.substr(loc->path.size()) is empty for GET /api and the emitted target is exactly the URI, so GET /api?cmd=whoami emits GET /exec?cmd=whoami HTTP/1.1 -- three tokens. A strict parser splits it, reads token 1 as the exec route with the attacker's query attached, and runs whoami. The bare form emits GET /exec HTTP/1.1 and runs id. The attacker contributes only a query string, so there is no decoder in the path to harden. Requires a proxy_pass URI naming the exec route with no trailing space and a location path the request matches exactly.
findings.title: Exact-match URI without a trailing space keeps a 3-token line, so an attacker query alone executes a chosen command on a strict parser

findings.description: The proxy waits for end+4+length bytes, consumes exactly that many, and writes the body after the header. A body containing a complete second request line is therefore presented to the upstream's parser as a body and executed a second time from one client request. Control: the same POST with a hello.txt body yields one upstream request and no second execution. Conversely a bodyless GET with a trailing request line and no Content-Length forwards nothing extra and the proxy closes, so the tail is lost; and Content-Length is rejected on non-proxy locations. Verified by raw upstream capture showing the whole body on the wire.
findings.title: A POST body is forwarded verbatim inside the proxied request, and a bodyless GET's tail is discarded, so only the POST form can carry a second request line

findings.description: HEAD is accepted on the proxy branch and the emitted first line is byte-identical to the GET form, so the upstream executes. The proxy then suppresses the response body, so the client sees Content-Length and zero bytes. It is a single-request execution but a two-request read. Verified: HEAD emitted HEAD /exec  HTTP/1.1 and the peer executed id; the client body length was 0; the following GET returned the uid output.
findings.title: HEAD with a split line executes upstream while the proxy returns zero body bytes; one later GET reads the output

findings.description: proxy_request parses one status line and bounds it to 100..599; a 1xx is not skipped. An upstream sending 100 Continue then a real response has the second response delivered as body text, and the proxy stamps the 1xx with a bogus reason phrase. The victim page then contains a complete nested response with its own Set-Cookie, which is a forgery primitive in front of the RCE. Verified with a peer emitting 100 then 200: the client received HTTP/1.1 100 Error with the 200 response as body.
findings.title: A 1xx upstream response is accepted as terminal, so an upstream nests a whole second response inside the victim body

findings.description: On the local branch the root is loc->s.alias and the subpath is path.substr(loc->path.size()), where path is decoded and the length is raw config text. A %2f inside the alias region decodes to one byte while the slice still measures the alias literal, shifting the walk one component. The per-component openat with O_NOFOLLOW keeps it inside the alias subtree, so this is a read-scope shift rather than an escape: a URL that looks like a different resource serves the shifted file. .. remains refused and a trailing slash on a regular file is 403. Verified with distinct marker files in the two roots.
findings.title: An alias location's slice is taken from the decoded path by a config length, so %2f changes which file under the alias root is served

limitations: One build only; the mechanism is shared with its siblings, which carry their own envelopes
The strict peer reproduces a generic 3-token request-line reader, not a named framework; SEC-001 also needs a whitespace-splitting upstream, which is stated per finding
SEC-006 is a read-scope shift under O_NOFOLLOW, not an escape to an arbitrary path
RCE is on the upstream host; the proxy process never executes code
No memory-safety fuzzing in this pass
methods: Read release/000002 source from the tag and confirmed its SHA-256 against release metadata
Built that exact source and confirmed --check-config accepts each probe config
Strict peer printing the upstream request line verbatim with a whitespace token count and firing sh only on an exact 3-token exec target
Same-config static control (GET /hello.txt) before every payload, and a /hello.txt body control for the POST case
Quoted-space, exact-match URI, POST-with-Content-Length, bodyless-GET-with-tail, HEAD, 1xx, alias and %2f-in-alias probes
Byte comparison of the upstream capture between control and payload

author_attested: analysis metadata reconstructed after the run
verified: release tag resolves to the submitted source
source SHA-256 and report and evidence hashes

scope: Second pass on final release release/000002 of stage-10 run 8d5ff1f2, source SHA-256 6acfccc3..., 98 lines. Config-shape axis of the proxy branch plus body framing, 1xx status handling and the alias local branch; each claim re-driven on a freshly compiled binary under a fresh config with a static control.
